**Nvidia** ( [NVDA](https://www.fool.com/quote/nasdaq/nvda/) +2.93%) has risen to become a leader in this area, and its advanced circuitry designs are enabling all sorts of high-end computing processes -- robots included. Nvidia chips also power everything from personal computers to small IoT devices to factory robotics.

With its advanced capabilities on the hardware _and_ software fronts, Nvidia is a top play in robotics for the long term, helping its customers unlock AI's power. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang believes robotics represents the company's second-biggest growth opportunity after AI. The company is working with several humanoid robot makers across the U.S., Europe, and Asia, with its Blackwell chips serving as the computing brains of these devices.

In June 2026, Nvidia announced Halos for robotics, the industry's first full-stack safety system for physical AI. By combining software, embedded systems, sensors, and silicon with industrial applications, Nvidia has developed a robotics safety ecosystem built for the scaled deployment of humanoid robots in factories, warehouses, and logistics operations.
